Text.Text: You stood at the end, and you came back up. Both matter; only one of them is rare. My vigil here is finished because of you. Carry the light gently. It is heavier than it looks.
There is courage in coming here. Bring your Force training to rank 50 before we go further. Courage needs something steady beneath it.

They still light the lamps in the Sith Crypt Depths. Six Last Stand of the Light adepts tend them, though the rite they serve has changed. Defeat the six and bring me their trial tablet. I want to know what remains of the words I taught them.
Take this key to the Crypt Depths entrance inside the Sith Crypt. Remember that you can leave. I wish I'd said that to my students sooner.

Because I led them here. Twelve students, seeking the oldest record of the last-stand rite, and I believed the crypts were only stone. The dark below was patient. I carry the ones I lost, and I keep this stair so it takes no one else unwatched. That is my penance and my post.
Enter the Sith Crypt on Korriban, then take the entrance marked for the Crypt Depths. The key I give you opens it. Bring your companions to the threshold together.

They will not run. They believe they are standing their last stand, and that belief makes them fearless. Six adepts, any one of them stronger than what you have faced in daylight. Do not let pity slow your blade, and do not let the crypt goad you into anger. Come back up. That is the only order I will give you.
Six adepts in the Sith Crypt Depths. Bring their tablet here to the Korriban Starport. I will wait for you.
You came back up. Good. That tablet in your hands taught them to call kneeling a stand. Give it to me and let it stop teaching.

It is done teaching lies. You moved well down there; I heard less screaming than I feared. Take the credits, they are all my purse can offer at this stair. The lesson beneath them matters more: you have seen how the rite fails. Next you will learn why.

Five specialists have bound the vigil to a ritual shard. They are drawing from it long after they should have stopped. Beat the five in the crypt depths and bring it to me. A light shouldn't have to consume someone to stay lit.
Carry the shard carefully. You don't owe it anything because you can feel it drawing on you.

A focus. In our practice it holds a guardian's calm, so the last one standing does not stand alone in their own mind. The fallen refilled it with fear. Every student who died afraid down there is still in it, feeding the rite. I want it in my hands so I can finally let them go.
Enter the Sith Crypt on Korriban, then take the entrance marked for the Crypt Depths. The key I give you opens it. Bring your companions to the threshold together.

Stronger, and quieter. The adepts performed; the specialists believe. Five of them, and they will not break formation to chase you. They will make you come to the shard, where they are strongest. Breathe, keep your guard honest, and remember that you are allowed to leave. The dead were not.
The five specialists in the crypt depths have the ritual shard. Recover it, then come back to me.
I can hear it in your pack. Softer than it was. You hurt the rite when you took it. Hand it to me. Some of my students are inside, and they have waited long enough.

Because it was coming home. There. They are quiet now, truly quiet, and that is the first mercy this place has allowed me. Take your pay, though I know you did not come for it. What waits deeper is worse. Rest first. Even light needs to close its eyes.

The warden guards the deeper vigil. Challenge him in the crypt depths and bring back his tomb sigil when he's defeated. I hope you'll ask others to come. There is no shame in having someone beside you at the hardest part.

Then gather them, and go down together. Do not spread out in the breach; he punishes whoever stands apart first. When it is over, close his eyes. He was mine before he was the crypt's, and I would have him rest looking at nothing worse than darkness.

Toma. He asked more questions than the rest of my students together, and every one was worth answering. When the crypt turned them, he did not kneel like the others. He planted himself at the tomb door and let the rite hollow him out standing up. The dark did not break his stand. It kept it. That is what you are walking into.
You've survived alone before. I'm glad. That doesn't oblige you to do it again. Another person can hold when you need to breathe, and remind you there is a way home. Ask someone, if you can.

The tomb seal he was sworn to keep whole. It splintered the night the deep doors were forced, and he wears the pieces like a vow he cannot put down. Bringing it to me will not mend the seal. It will let me finish his watch for him, the way someone should have finished mine.
Call the warden at the crypt depths' challenge marker. Defeat him and return his tomb sigil.
You closed his eyes. I can see it in how quietly you are standing. Give me the sigil, and give yourself a moment. Both are earned.

Then he finally kept his oath, and you helped him keep it. I will carry these splinters up into the sun, where a seal like this belongs. You have done what I could not, twice now. What remains below is the circle that turned them, and the one who taught the turning. Sleep before you let yourself hate them. It helps.

Four keepers still hold the rite token. They decide who must stand the vigil and who is allowed to leave it. Defeat the four in the crypt depths and recover that token. I would like those choices returned to the people making them.
Bring the rite token here. Let the keepers' claims end with their vigil.

Not my students. Older. They were down there before I brought anyone, waiting the way a snare waits. They studied our last-stand rite through the walls and rewrote it so that surrender looks like courage. My students only failed to see the difference. The keepers made certain the difference was hard to see.

Permission. Whoever bears it may lead the rite and choose who stands and who is spent. They pass it hand to hand when a vigil changes. Take it, and no keeper can pass the rite forward. It dies with them. That is why it must be all four, and why they will defend it past sense.

I would. Four keepers do not stand politely in a row. They scatter and reform like smoke, and one of them will always be behind you. You know your strength better than I do now. Just keep the rule that has brought you back twice: come home. Everything else is preference.
Four keepers in the crypt depths still have the rite token. Bring it here when their vigil ends.
The stone feels lighter. That sounds like madness above ground; down here it is simply true. The token, please. Let me hold the thing that decided what my students became.

Four vigils, ended. I thought I would feel triumph. Mostly I hear how quiet it is. Take your pay, and take this truth with it: everything below is finished except the one who began it. The master still stands at the bottom of the dark, and the stand he keeps is the very thing you came here to learn. When you are ready, come whisper with me one last time.

The master waits in the Final Ritual Chamber. Call him at the challenge marker and defeat him. He will ask more of you than anyone can give. Leave yourself something for the journey home. I'll be here at the starport when you return.

Then go down one last time. Watch each other more than you watch him. His stand does not break from the front; it breaks when the people beside you refuse to fall. When his ends, keep yours. And come home. I will be listening the whole way.

It means being the reason someone else keeps breathing when everything says stop. Not glory. Not defiance for its own sake. A door that holds because you decided it holds. He knows the form of it perfectly and the reason not at all. That is your one advantage, and it is real. You have people to hold the door for. He only has the door.

I do not know his name, and I have stood at this stair for years. The keepers called him only the master. He took our rite whole, the stance, the breath, the refusal to fall, and cut away everyone it was for. What remains is a stand with no one behind it, kept for its own sake in the dark. It cannot end on its own. Endings are the one thing he no longer knows how to do.

No. And it costs me to say so. My vigil is this stair. If I leave it, what climbs out while we are all below? I will hold the way open and the way home lit. That is my stand. Yours is at the bottom. When it is done, come up slowly, all three of you, and let me count your footsteps. It is the only prayer I have left.
The Final Ritual Chamber holds the master's challenge marker. Defeat him, then come back to the starport. Save strength for that, too.
Three sets of footsteps. All climbing. I have waited years at this stair to hear that, and I did not know it until now. Tell me it is done.
You've come back. Let that be enough for tonight. Your pay is here. When you're rested, I can teach you Last Stand of the Light. I will ask you to endure, but I will always want you to come home.
Tell me the task again, quietly.
Quietly, then. Six adepts, and the tablet.
Why does a Jedi keep vigil here, of all places?
How do I reach them?
What will they do when they see me?
Not yet. Let me prepare.
Take it. It's heavier than stone should be.
Back to the shard.
Five specialists, one shard. I'll bring it up.
What is the shard, exactly?
Where do the specialists keep it?
Are they stronger than the adepts?
Not tonight.
Here. It stopped pulsing on the stairs.
Back to the warden.
I'll end his vigil.
Who was he, before?
Why bring others? I've fought alone before.
And the sigil?
I need to gather my people first.
He stood until the end. Here's the sigil.
Back to the keepers.
All four keepers. It ends there.
Who are the keepers?
What does the token mean to them?
Should I bring my companions again?
Give me a little time.
The circle is finished. Take their token.
Back to the master.
We'll stand together. All the way down.
Tell me what standing at the end really means.
What is he now?
Will you come down with us?
Not until my companions are ready.
It's done. His stand is ended, and we're all still standing.
